purpose: Start Week 1 matchup shadow calibration by screening every active game from the existing market-isolated personnel ledger, opening only evidence-supported opponent-specific cases and leaving all matchup point increments null until a separate numeric calibration is justified.

candidateEvidence.opponentStressPlayerOrUnit: Arizona pass rush led by starting OLB Josh Sweat
candidateEvidence.footballMechanism: Tyler Biadasz was acquired in part for center-specific A-gap protection, space-blocking and communication responsibilities in Mike McDaniel's offense. His season-ending ACL injury moves rookie Jake Slaughter into the starting center role. Arizona's current official depth chart lists Josh Sweat as a starting OLB, and Cardinals reporting identifies Sweat as the pass-rush leader after a 12-sack 2025 season. That combination is sufficient to open a shadow protection-cascade case for opponent-specific review, but it is not sufficient by itself to invent a point multiplier or matchup increment.
candidateEvidence.note: Open the case only. The normal governed personnel loss remains the sole numeric effect until M2 numeric calibration separately approves an increment.
